## About Ternux

Ternux turns an ARM64 Android phone into a Linux desktop without rooting or
replacing Android. Termux hosts the Linux guest in PRoot, Termux:X11 displays
the Xfce desktop, and PulseAudio connects guest audio to Android. A single CLI
installs and manages guest systems, desktop sessions, graphics, diagnostics,
and optional workloads.

The desktop comes with everyday tools for browsing, documents, media, photos,
and audio recording, alongside Ternux's branded theme and phone-sized window
handling. Developer tools and local CPU/Vulkan AI workloads are available as
optional installs. Guest files and model weights can be read from Android
shared storage when Termux storage access is enabled.

**Debian, Ubuntu and Alpine are the three v2-supported desktop profiles.** The
physical-device evidence represents the Redmi Turbo 4 Pro / Android 16 / Adreno
825; see the feature matrix and current audit for the exact tested scope.
Debian is the recommended default. Twelve additional named distro recipes are
available to try, but are not qualified for the v2 desktop support promise;
arbitrary OCI images are shell guests until a Ternux desktop recipe is added.

### Graphics and guest support

All 15 named recipes include distro-specific Mesa GL packages. On Adreno/KGSL,
Ternux prefers the guest's supported Zink/Freedreno path; Debian Trixie also has
a validated Turnip payload. VirGL is the compatibility route. The selected
renderer depends on the device and Android graphics stack, so check it with
`glxinfo -B` inside the guest.

## Install

1. Install [Termux from F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux/) or
   [Termux GitHub releases](https://github.com/termux/termux-app/releases), and the
   [Termux:X11 nightly app](https://github.com/termux/termux-x11/releases/tag/nightly)
   from compatible sources. The nightly app enables each concurrently running
   guest to open in its own Android window when selected with `tx start NAME`;
   older X11 apps fall back to one shared window. Open Termux:X11 once.
   For better foreground/background CPU scheduling while X11 is open, GitHub
   Termux users can choose the upstream
   [shared-UID debug APK](https://github.com/termux/termux-x11/releases/tag/nightly)
   (`termux-x11-universal-sharedUid-debug.apk`). It runs under Termux's shared
   Android UID so Android is less likely to throttle the Linux workload when
   Termux is behind X11. This APK requires the GitHub-signed Termux app; with
   F-Droid or Google Play Termux, use the standard
   [`termux-x11-universal-debug.apk`](https://github.com/termux/termux-x11/releases/tag/nightly).
   Optional companion apps: [Termux:Boot on F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux.boot/)
   or [GitHub](https://github.com/termux/termux-boot/releases) starts configured
   scripts after reboot; [Termux:API on F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux.api/)
   or [GitHub](https://github.com/termux/termux-api/releases) adds Android
   utilities (also install `pkg install termux-api`); and [Termux:Styling on
   F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux.styling/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/termux/termux-styling/releases)
   adds terminal themes and fonts. Ternux desktop apps capture live microphone audio
   on demand through Termux's OpenSL ES source; the API's recorder is file-based.
   Install Termux and its add-ons from the same source.
2. In Termux, run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/soobujmiah/ternux/main/install.sh | bash
```

If `curl` is unavailable, use:

```bash
wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/soobujmiah/ternux/main/install.sh | bash
```

If neither downloader can run, repair Termux packages first with
`apt update && apt full-upgrade`, then retry. A partial upgrade can leave curl
unable to load its OpenSSL libraries; running `pkg update` before completing
the upgrade can reproduce that mismatch.

The Ternux v2.0.0 GitHub release and stable APT distribution were withdrawn
on 2026-11-14. The `v2.0.0` source tag remains available for provenance. Use
the source installer above; the signed `/apt-rc` channel remains for opt-in
candidate testing and is not a production install source. The next stable release
remains in the v2 major. The planned v3 platform architecture and acceptance
gates are now required for the next 2.x release; no stable release will be
published until they pass.
See the [APT channel status](docs/TERMUX-APT.md) and [v2 release record](docs/V2-RELEASE-READINESS.md).

The base install needs about 4–4.6 GB of storage. Keep extra temporary space for
downloads and package caches.

## Start and use

In Termux, start the desktop:

```bash
source ~/.bashrc
x
```

Switch to the Termux:X11 app to see Xfce. Common commands, all run in Termux:

```bash
tx status         # short alias for the Ternux CLI
ternux verify     # verify the active guest; use verify db/ub/alp to choose
ternux doctor     # diagnose common problems
tx stop           # choose one/many running guest desktops
tx distro list    # show every installed PRoot guest
tx distro search alpine # search available OCI images
tx distro uninstall NAME # remove a Ternux-managed guest
```

Use `tx stop --all` to close every managed Ternux desktop. With the Termux:X11 nightly app, each Ternux desktop guest gets its own tagged Android window and separate settings; `tx start db`, `tx start ub`, or `tx start alp` brings the selected window forward. Older X11 apps use one shared window and cannot reliably switch among concurrently running guests. Install multiple profiles with `tx install --distros debian,ubuntu,alpine`; each receives the family-matched Ternux base desktop. `xgo` lists every installed guest and asks which desktop to start when there is more than one. Generic images without a Ternux package recipe are shown as shell-only. See [the release-readiness report](docs/V2-RELEASE-READINESS.md) for the exact v2 scope, evidence, and publication status.

The `x` shortcut starts the saved desktop; `xgo` opens Termux:X11 and asks which installed desktop guest to start. `tx` is the short CLI command. Use `db`/`dbr`/`dbroot`, `ub`/`ubr`/`ubroot`, `alp`/`alpr`/`alproot`, `archx`/`archroot`, `fed`/`fedr`, `suse`/`suser`, `vsh`/`vroot`, or `kal`/`kalr` for the corresponding user/root shells when those guests are installed. Start Ubuntu or Alpine with `tx start ub` or `tx start alp` (full names also work). Use `tx distro shell NAME` to enter a profile’s configured regular user (generic images keep their image default), or `tx distro exec NAME -- COMMAND` for any installed PRoot guest. Root remains explicit through `dbroot`, `ubroot`, `alproot` and the matching root aliases. Search PRoot-Distro images with `tx distro search QUERY`; install a generic OCI image with `tx distro image-install IMAGE[:TAG] [NAME]`. Generic images provide guest shells. Named distro profiles use the matching package-manager recipe; arbitrary OCI images provide guest shells until a family recipe is added. Android shared storage is mounted at `/sdcard` in every managed guest by default, so
models and files are available directly. Termux must have Android storage permission;
use `termux-setup-storage` once if `/sdcard` is missing.

## What you get

**Base desktop:** Debian 13 (Trixie) by default, or another named package-family recipe, in user-space PRoot with Xfce4,
Termux:X11 display integration, and PulseAudio audio routing. The Debian/Ubuntu APT profile
includes Bangla-capable Noto fonts and Avro phonetic input (Ctrl+Space). Alpine
uses a checksum-pinned IBus m17n Avro phonetic engine because its stable APK
repositories do not package that engine. Ctrl+Space cycles English and Bangla; Ternux syncs IBus's engine order with the preload list and adds an XFCE fallback for apps without an IBus input context. A shared X11 window-fit service keeps new windows inside each guest's phone-sized work area. No extra keyboard button is added to the panel. The base desktop includes VLC,
PulseAudio Volume Control, Xfce Task Manager, Mousepad, Galculator, Evince PDF
reader, Ternux Camera, Ternux Sound Recorder,
Ristretto image viewer, and Firefox browser. Debian-family APT guests also include Synaptic Package Manager, which uses Ternux branding and manages guest packages. App availability follows each distro family; optional workloads currently target APT guests. Evince is
the default PDF reader; LibreOffice Draw is optional for editing PDF pages and exporting documents to other formats.
Celestia is available as an optional astronomy simulator and is not installed by default. No mail client is installed or set as default. Evolution is available as an optional
mail client; common providers can use OAuth, and other hosts support manual IMAP/POP
setup. Firefox is installed in every fresh guest and handles OAuth in the guest;
the Android default browser remains the fallback. One-click Camera, Photos, and Sound Recorder shortcuts
are on the Xfce panel. Qt5 applications such as VLC use the matching GTK platform theme. The systemwide graphite-and-emerald Ternux GTK theme covers apps, menus,
and panel; custom Ternux Xfwm frames cover window borders and title bars. GTK client-side titlebar buttons, including Firefox controls, use visible Ternux styling. The
Ternux icon theme uses original app, folder, Thunar-action, category, and panel
icons, plus branded aliases for optional GUI apps such as Blender, GIMP,
Krita, Inkscape, Audacity, Geany, and LibreOffice; Evince is a base app; Evolution has a branded icon when selected from optional software. Thunar actions have their own
icon context. Adwaita remains the neutral fallback for uncommon or newly installed apps;
Papirus is not inherited. Fifteen selectable portrait-first branded wallpapers preserve
their proportions in landscape. Ternux Camera lists
Android front/rear cameras and captures photos through Termux:API after Camera
permission is granted to the Termux:API app. Each photo appears in the app preview after capture with its EXIF orientation corrected; compact controls fit the window. Photos save in the active guest at `~/Pictures/Ternux`. A validated capture is staged in Termux app storage, then copied into PRoot; no Gallery scan is performed. Ristretto is the
default image viewer. Termux:API provides still-photo capture; it does not expose a continuous camera stream for live preview.
Ternux Sound Recorder captures only after you press Start. Save as AAC/M4A by default, or choose MP3; MP3 is encoded with the guest FFmpeg. Recordings stay in the active guest at `~/Music/Ternux`.

A one-time first-run welcome opens the project website in the included Firefox ESR.
Ubuntu uses Mozilla’s official ESR build because Ubuntu’s archive Firefox package
requires Snap, which Ternux disables in PRoot.

**Graphics:** every named desktop recipe installs its distro's Mesa GL driver
and a GPU route. On Adreno/KGSL, auto prefers native distro Mesa Zink and
Freedreno where packages exist; Debian Trixie uses the tested direct Zink +
Turnip stack. VirGL is the compatibility route through the Android host graphics
stack. Hardware acceleration depends on the guest packages, device and Android
build. Use `ternux verify` and `glxinfo -B` inside the guest to inspect the
renderer; opening a desktop alone does not prove hardware acceleration. `ternux gpu` and `ternux backend` inspect and manage the route. See
[graphics persistence](docs/GRAPHICS-PERSISTENCE.md).

**Optional software:** the interactive installer lets you choose individual
packages or workload groups. Choices include developer toolchains and editors,
Android SDK/NDK tools, Firefox, local AI runtimes, network
utilities, media and graphics apps, office tools, and Blender. The base install
stays smaller; choose only what you need. The `--all` profile needs roughly
10.5–12.5 GB installed and about 14 GB free during setup. See
[workload details](docs/WORKLOADS.md).

**Local AI and GPU tools:** optional extensions provide llama.cpp CPU + Vulkan,
plus a pinned Stable Diffusion CPU + Vulkan image generator preview; install
with `ternux extension install llama-vulkan` or
`ternux extension install stable-diffusion`. Model weights stay outside the runtime and can be used straight from shared
storage. The separate Hexagon HTP extension remains
experimental and device-specific. Blender and headless EEVEE tools are optional.
See the [llama.cpp extension guide](guides/llama-vulkan-extension.md) for
model setup and memory-conscious context settings. The [Stable Diffusion guide](guides/stable-diffusion-vulkan-extension.md)
and [release plan](docs/ACCELERATOR-RELEASE-PLAN.md) cover current support limits
and qualification gates.

## Manage and troubleshoot

The CLI can start, stop and restart a managed background desktop; report
session, device and install state; run diagnostics and safe repair; verify the
installation; inspect or update the graphics backend; capture GPU benchmarks
and device profiles; view logs; update Ternux; manage extensions; and remove
selected components. Commands support help, and documented commands also offer
machine-readable JSON.

```bash
ternux info             # device and system summary
ternux logs desktop tail # recent desktop log
ternux gpu status        # graphics driver status
ternux --help            # command list
```

See the [CLI reference](docs/CLI.md), [daily use](docs/USAGE.md), and
[troubleshooting guide](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for exact behavior. Android
memory pressure and vendor battery policies can still stop long-running PRoot
sessions; Ternux reports diagnostics but cannot override every device policy.

For Android app development on this same device, install ADT inside the Ternux
Debian guest. The build-to-device workflow is validated on the shared Termux +
PRoot host; use from inside the Ternux Xfce session is not formally tested yet.
See the [ADT setup steps](docs/INSTALLATION.md#install-adt-tools-inside-the-ternux-debian-guest)
and [ADT + Ternux notes](https://github.com/soobujmiah/adt/blob/main/docs/TERNUX_RELATIONSHIP.md).

For Blender work, coding agents can use Ternux's local GPU MCP to check the
render route and run scripts or scenes with the documented EEVEE setup. See the
[MCP guide](tools/blender-gpu-mcp/README.md) and [render evidence](experiments/cartoon-pipeline/README.md).

## More help

- [Ternux v3 architecture and implementation roadmap](docs/v3/README.md):
  native manager (native workspace `:0`; Debian/Ubuntu/Alpine `:1`/`:2`/`:3`
  by design), workspaces, compute, AI, Device Bridge, security, and gates.
  Four read-only manager CLI commands and an explicit foreground Unix-socket
  service are in the current source checkout; they are not in the withdrawn
  v2.0.0 package. The native Control Center UI and service supervision are
  required before the next v2-major stable release.
- [Current project status](docs/project/PROJECT-ROADMAP.md): implementation,

- [Benchmarks](docs/BENCHMARKS.md): measured device results and their limits.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

With a terminal attached, the installer first offers a keyboard checklist for
one or more guest profiles (Space/number toggles, Enter confirms), then a
categorized keyboard checklist for optional software; Space or item numbers
toggle multiple choices, Enter reviews the plan, and `q` keeps the base desktop.
`--yes` skips prompts and installs the Debian base profile, while explicit
`--with-*` flags or `--all` select additional workloads. The v2.0.0 GitHub
release and stable APT distribution were withdrawn on 2026-11-14; its source tag
and package checksums remain in the historical [release report](docs/V2-RELEASE-REPORT.md).
The next stable release remains in the v2 major. The Control Center and the full
platform scope formerly planned for v3 are required for the next 2.x release;
see the [architecture dossier](docs/V3-ARCHITECTURE.md) and [current roadmap]
(docs/project/PROJECT-ROADMAP.md).
Current source has four read-only `tx manager` commands and `tx manager serve`
for a foreground-only local Unix-socket API. A background supervisor and
graphical Control Center are not implemented yet. See the [APT channel status](docs/TERMUX-APT.md).
HTP/HMX,
QNN and wider accelerator qualification remain experimental or follow-up work;
see the [accelerator plan](docs/ACCELERATOR-RELEASE-PLAN.md).
